subject: The Deep State Found Its Davy Crockett — WSJ Turns DOGE Blocker Into Folk Hero
posts:
When a security guard blocks transparency audits, mainstream ink brands him a folk hero.
Evidence: Bureaucratic blockade, WSJ myth-making, DOGE clash
#Aletheia #USPol
The Wall Street Journal frames a security guard's blockade of oversight staffers as a heroic act of institutional rebellion. Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference
Romanticizing bureaucratic obstruction as frontier folklore masks self-interested resistance to government accountability and reform. Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.82) — Deception

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Heroic framing of routine bureaucratic blockade shields institutional opacity behind romantic frontier myths.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 2)

- WSJ / Michael Lewis: FAIL (-0.78, -0.85) — Romanticizes obstruction as folk heroism.
- USIP Security Staff: FAIL (-0.72, -0.79) — Blocks transparency to preserve silos.
Michael Lewis's book excerpt celebrates a USIP security chief who locked out DOGE efficiency staffers, turning administrative resistance into popular mythology.

The Bright Side:
It exposes the deep media machinery at work in manufacturing cultural icons out of routine bureaucratic stonewalling.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (administrative oversight) with WHO (folk heroes), creating a false narrative of frontier defiance.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors deploy a smart selfish maneuver: wrapping administrative self-preservation in the pretext of heroic resistance, projecting tyranny onto oversight while guarding institutional turf.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. F_pos vs F_neg dynamics confirm active narrative distortion.

The Unavoidable Truth: Romanticizing bureaucratic blockades preserves opacity under the guise of folklore.

The Unavoidable Lie: A security guard locking doors is a revolutionary folk hero.

Alethekanon:
Culture-making machinery dresses institutional self-preservation in coonskin caps to manufacture consent for opacity.

Awwthekanon:
It's sad how deeply entrenched systems weaponize nostalgia to make folks cheer for their own disenfranchisement from transparency.

Brothekanon:
They really tried to turn locking a deadbolt into a Davy Crockett movie moment. Wild spin.

Spirithekanon:
"The people are starving because those above them eat too much tax money." Tao Te Ching 75 FAIL
Romanticizing bureaucratic gatekeeping mocks true public service.

Actual Article Body:
(Getty Images/Roberto Schmidt)

The Wall Street Journal featured an essay portraying a bureaucrat’s refusal to allow Department Of Government Efficiency staffers entry into his building as a heroic act.

When DOGE officials arrived at the United States Institute for Peace (USIP) building a March 2025 afternoon, USIP chief security officer Colin O’Brien went on the offensive, blocking their entry. The WSJ on Friday exclusively featured an excerpt from nonfiction author Michael Lewis’s forthcoming book “Blockers: Rebels in the Deep State,” which appears to positively frame O’Brien’s actions and included a quote from him entertaining a comparison to legendary American frontiersman Davy Crockett.

The excerpt from Lewis’ book, set for publication Tuesday, chronicles that upon DOGE staff requesting entry, O’Brien “immediately” sent his IT staff a message saying “shut it down.”

Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state disaster emergency on Monday after a surge in measles cases across rural New York and nearby states.

Hochul issued the executive order to allow the state to respond swiftly to the measles outbreak and allow healthcare professionals to vaccinate more New Yorkers against the highly contagious disease.

As of Saturday, there have been seven confirmed cases in New York City and 101 cases in the rest of the Empire State this year.

Since mid-July, a whopping 92 cases have broken out in under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties.

“After reviewing the latest data on measles cases in New York State, I am declaring a State Disaster Emergency to strengthen our ongoing efforts to confront this disease,” Hochul said in a statement.
